description: Water, the deep Earth, wind, fire and human activity are used to explain how planetary systems shaped the rise and direction of civilizations.

s03e01.description: From Iceland to the Middle East and India, Stewart shows how societies succeeded by locating, controlling and adapting to freshwater systems whose availability constantly shifts with geography and climate.

s03e02.description: Crystal caves, desert fissures and ancient tunnels reveal why civilizations repeatedly clustered near fault zones, gaining access to valuable resources while accepting the geological danger beneath them.

s03e03.description: A journey across oceans and deserts traces the hidden global patterns of wind, showing how atmospheric circulation powered travel, trade and decisive turning points in human history.

s03e04.description: Stewart follows humanity’s dependence on fire and stored energy, linking geology to industrial development and showing why different resource landscapes pushed Britain and China along different historical paths.

s03e05.description: The final chapter turns to humanity itself as a geological force, examining how extensively people now alter Earth’s natural cycles and what responsibility comes with that unprecedented influence.
